aggressive_definition: Incident advanced prostate cancer and fatal prostate cancer were analyzed as aggressive endpoints; nonadvanced prostate cancer was analyzed separately.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: the authors identified 10,180 total prostate cancer cases (8,754 nonadvanced, 1,426 advanced, and 178 fatal cases).
study_design: Prospective NIH-AARP Diet and Health cohort analysis using baseline dietary assessment and Cox regression during up to six years of follow-up.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: During up to 6 years of follow-up (n = 293,888), the authors identified 10,180 total prostate cancer cases (8,754 nonadvanced, 1,426 advanced, and 178 fatal cases).
reason: The study analyzed total incident prostate cancer and separately reported nonadvanced, advanced, and fatal prostate cancer. Advanced and fatal disease qualify as aggressive incident endpoints.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Skim milk, but not other dairy foods, was associated with increased risk of advanced prostate cancer (> or = 2 vs. zero servings/day: RR = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.99, 1.54; p(trend) = 0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns incident advanced prostate cancer.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In contrast, calcium from nondairy foods was associated with lower risk of nonadvanced prostate cancer (> or = 600 vs. < 250 mg/day: RR = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.68, 0.99; p(trend) = 0.04).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly for nonadvanced prostate cancer and therefore is not an aggressive endpoint.

additional_estimates.comparison: > or = 2,000 vs. 500-<750 mg/day of total calcium
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: However, a statistically nonsignificant positive association with total calcium was observed for advanced (> or = 2,000 vs. 500-<750 mg/day: relative risk (RR) = 1.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.91, 1.71; p(trend) = 0.06) and fatal (> or = 1,000 vs. 500-<750 mg/day: RR = 1.39, 95% CI: 0.92, 2.09; p(trend) = 0.10) prostate cancer.
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: During up to 6 years of follow-up (n = 293,888), the authors identified 10,180 total prostate cancer cases (8,754 nonadvanced, 1,426 advanced, and 178 fatal cases).
